_comment: Human corrections to the distance-derived facility grouping in
assign_facilities.py. The 60m rule guesses, and these are the cases where a
'merge' forces the listed court IDs into one facility at any distance — for a
park whose surfaces sit further apart than the threshold.
'split' forces a court onto its own facility — for two places the threshold
wrongly pooled, such as courts either side of a street.
A court ID in both loses: split wins. A wrongly-merged facility silently pools
two parks' queues, a wrongly-split one only shows two pins.
Court IDs come from courts.json. An ID here that no longer exists in the
dataset is reported as a warning, not an error, so a dataset rebuild that
drops a court doesn't break the run.
